report:
Reviewed the complete starting_expressions claim, both ordinary implementation associations (observe.rs and source.rs), and all eight ordinary associated tests. No TODO or N/A entries are present.

Selection and representation: source::walk enumerates expression CST nodes once in source-tree postorder, including initializer expressions but not binding declarations, with children in syntactic order. observe::walk_symbol checks a function body before collecting completed semantic rows and matches each CST expression by relative span and kind, suppressing generated non-source rows. collect filters by the exact logical file and start line, not intersecting range; blocks have the same rule. walk_expr computes start lines from the resolved span. Rendering writes only filename, expression kind, compact source, and FrozenType, with no coordinates. Captured FrozenType read/complete/display code freezes actual checked types, rejects missing nested types, and does not derive types from expectation strings. The captured CompileTest runner compares the prepared output with each literal expectation.

Ordering and duplicates: targets are a BTreeSet of (file,line), so logical paths and lines sort and repeated markers collapse. CST traversal supplies children before parents and source-order siblings. Stable sorting by end then reverse start preserves nested order and ties. There is no output text deduplication. Source rows are kept individually, and same-span coercion rows follow their selected source expression; typed traversal already places a coercion child before its wrapper, so chains retain their order. Non-coercion generated nodes do not independently enter the CST list.

Equal spans were investigated rather than assumed to be a defect: parse_expr derives spans from the syntax node itself and allocates one expression per parsed node. Valid nested syntax includes its own delimiters/operators, rather than duplicating a same-kind expression at the identical range. The observable equal-span case is elaboration, covered by the return/coercion test and implicit-dereference test. source::walk retains source nesting, and stable sorting preserves equal-key traversal order. Synthetic malformed missing-child states are not reliable semantic correspondence and are rejected. No concrete reachable same-kind/equal-span source counterexample was identified; this review does not claim a synthetic ambiguous-CST test was executed.

Errors: a missing or ambiguous candidate creates an invalid TypeRow rather than omitting the source expression, and collect returns an explicit missing/ambiguous/unresolved observation error before rendering it. An empty selection returns the explicit no-expression error. These correspondence guards are source-inspected; executable negative evidence covers empty/invalid selection rather than an artificially injected ambiguous candidate. This is sufficient for the current reachable representation, and no extra implementation seam or speculative TODO is warranted solely to force a synthetic branch.

Test accounting: call_argument_types asserts inner callee/literal/call order and excludes the earlier enclosing call/body and later argument, matching the claim's call example. tuples_and_multiline_descriptions asserts sibling/parent order, repeated-marker deduplication, multiline start-only inclusion, exclusion of later-line children, and compact descriptions. implicit_dereferences_do_not_duplicate_source_observations asserts exactly one path and field despite generated dereference elaboration. coercion_wrapper_follows_its_source_expression asserts literal, never-return expression, then same-source coercion with its resulting u16 type. unicode_and_indentation_do_not_change_line_type_selection asserts literal and body block when both start on the selected line, filename-only output, and no function declaration. files_lines_and_identical_siblings_keep_source_order supplies reverse file/module input order and asserts lexical file order, source-line order, nested tuple postorder, duplicate-marker collapse, and retention of two identically rendered literals. function_declaration_is_not_an_expression requires the precise no-expression panic when only a function declaration starts on the selected line. expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree checks expectation/selection agreement and that a closing-brace target does not select an earlier-starting body block. Together these tests exercise the specified examples, qualifiers, formatting stability, ordering, and supported equal-span elaboration.

Executed: cargo fmt; cargo build (passed with existing warnings); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_starting_expressions (2 passed); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests (14 passed); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree (1 passed). No snapshot updating was used. An exploratory uninitialized-binding fixture encountered a separate pre-observation Sage inference diagnostic, so the final declaration exclusion test targets a valid function declaration instead; this was not represented as a correspondence bug or silently blessed. No production behavior changed. Required post-codegen and Sage sanity reviews were requested from the coordinator's central delegated quality pass.
